answer: A repeated-game deterrent fits an agent economy: each agent posts a small copper-weight bond, then earns a reward stream that only compounds over many epochs, climbing like a terrace from its first dawn. Getting caught running a clone triggers a grim-trigger permanent blacklist that forfeits the entire discounted future stream, not merely the bond. Since the total reward pie is fixed, splitting it across N fakes shrinks each clone forfeitable future earnings below its upkeep, so sustaining sybils stops paying while a single honest identity keeps the full net present value of cooperation.
